heard: You do not need 25,000 miles per hour to escape Earth. That terrifying speed limit is actually just a mathematical shortcut for a single unpowered ballistic burst. If you fire a projectile and let gravity do all the work, you genuinely need 11.2 kilometers per second. But spacecraft are not simple cannonballs. By keeping their powerful engines burning, they can climb slowly at a leisurely walking pace and still slip away completely. Escape velocity is not a strict speed limit you must break, but merely an underlying energy bill. Thanks to continuous thrust provided by onboard propellants, you never have to pay that massive bill all at once.
